blocks.content: Waves are generated mainly by wind. Their erosional power depends on height, frequency, and fetch (distance over which wind blows).

blocks.content: Waves are generated mainly by wind.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Waves are primarily generated by the force of wind acting on the water surface.
Wave erosional power is determined by height, frequency, and fetch.
Swash pushes water forward onto the shore, while backwash pulls it back into the sea.
Longshore drift moves coastal sediments in a characteristic zigzag path.

rows: Forward movement of water onto shore
Return flow of water to sea

blocks.content: • Swash – forward movement of water onto shore.
• Backwash – return flow of water to sea.

items: Questions often contrast Swash (forward flow onto shore) with Backwash (return flow to sea).
Fetch is strictly defined as the distance over which wind travels over water.
Longshore drift is frequently tested as the mechanism responsible for the zigzag transport of sediment.

blocks.content: • Fetch – distance wind travels over water.
• Longshore Drift – zigzag movement of sediments along the coast.
